newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end lower, but keep above key level.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end lower, but keep above key level.

text.p: Swiss shares ended lower but kept above the psychologically important level of 5,000 points in the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI), while the shares of Swiss Bank Corp (SBC) and ABB Asea Brown Boveri posted strong gains.
Weakness in index-heavyweights Roche and Novartis put pressure on the whole market, dealers said.
"But all in all, it was surprising how well we held our own despite the U.S. dollar's weakness," one dealer said.
The SMI ended 12.1 points down, or 0.24 percent, at 5,003.9 while the all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) ended up 0.54 points, or 0.02 percent, to 3,167.82.
Further development was seen depending on Wall Street.
One dealer said there were fears that some big investors that favoured the Swiss bourse at the start of the year may pull out due to its recent record-breaking performance.

SBC was the winner of the day in blue chips, rocketing 11 francs, or 3.33 percent, to 341 francs. The bank today said net profit for the first quarter was clearly above expectations, seen as the most optimistic statement yet by a major Swiss bank.
ABB added 34 francs to 1,887, helped by talk of a favourable study.
CS Group also posted gains, while UBS bearers gave up initial gains to end down four francs to 1,400.
Shares of Swiss National Bank continued to soar on speculative buying, jumping 370 francs to 2,090.
Roche, which payed out a dividend of 75 francs on its certificates today, slid 220 francs to 12,680 on profit taking.
Novartis registereds gave up 10 francs ot 1,980.
Among insurers, Winterthur made a strong showing, adding 23 francs to 1,110. Holderbank rose 22 francs to 1,232.
